title: Scope: the Distinguishing Aₙ-Generator, Not Full Generation
content: This entry identifies and characterizes the Vandermonde/discriminant polynomial Δ = ∏_{i<j}(xⱼ - xᵢ) as the generating invariant that separates the alternating-group invariants R[x]^{Aₙ} from the symmetric invariants R[e₁,…,eₙ]. It proves Δ is alternating, an Aₙ-invariant, not symmetric (so Δ ∉ R[e₁,…,eₙ]), has square in R[e₁,…,eₙ], and has degree n(n-1)/2. It does NOT prove the full generation statement R[x]^{Aₙ} = R[e₁,…,eₙ][Δ] (recorded as the open question). The alternating law, Aₙ-invariance and Δ²-symmetry hold over an infinite integral domain; non-symmetry additionally needs 2 ≠ 0 and n ≥ 2 (necessarily — in characteristic 2, alternating = symmetric). 0 axioms, 0 sorries; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

title: Reducing Δ to the Vandermonde Determinant
content: The whole argument runs through evaluation. eval_vandermondePoly shows eval v Δ = det (vandermonde v): eval is a ring homomorphism, so it distributes over the double product ∏_i ∏_{j∈Ioi i}(X j - X i), matching Matrix.det_vandermonde's formula ∏_i ∏_{j∈Ioi i}(v j - v i) term by term. vandermonde_comp_perm shows that precomposing the point v with a permutation e is a row permutation of the matrix: vandermonde (v ∘ e) = (vandermonde v).submatrix e id, which holds entrywise by rfl since both sides are (v (e i))^j. These two bridge lemmas import the classical determinant machinery into the polynomial world.

title: The Alternating Law via eval + funext
content: The structural core: rename e Δ = sign(e) • Δ. Classically this is proved by tracking how a permutation reorders the factors of ∏_{i<j}(xⱼ-xᵢ) — a delicate sign bookkeeping. Here it is obtained for free: eval_rename_vandermondePoly combines MvPolynomial.eval_rename (renaming = precomposition of the point) with Matrix.det_permute (a row permutation scales the determinant by the sign) to get eval v (rename e Δ) = sign(e) • eval v Δ for EVERY point v; then MvPolynomial.funext — valid over an infinite integral domain — upgrades this pointwise identity to the polynomial identity. Aₙ-invariance (vandermondePoly_isInvariant_of_sign_eq_one) is the sign = 1 case; Δ²-symmetry (vandermondePoly_sq_isSymmetric) is sign² = 1, presenting the Aₙ-invariants as a degree-two extension of the Sₙ-invariants.

title: Δ Is a Genuinely New Generator (2 ≠ 0 Is Essential)
content: vandermondePoly_ne_zero: Δ ≠ 0, because at an injective tuple v (available since R is infinite) the Vandermonde determinant is nonzero (det_vandermonde_ne_zero_iff). vandermondePoly_not_isSymmetric: a transposition e = swap i0 i1 has sign(e) = -1, so eval v (rename e Δ) = -eval v Δ; if Δ were symmetric this equals eval v Δ, forcing -x = x, i.e. 2x = 0 with x = eval v Δ ≠ 0 — impossible in a domain with 2 ≠ 0. vandermondePoly_not_mem_symmetricSubalgebra then converts non-symmetry to Δ ∉ R[e₁,…,eₙ] via mem_symmetricSubalgebra. The characteristic hypothesis 2 ≠ 0 is necessary: in characteristic 2, alternating collapses to symmetric and Δ IS symmetric.

title: Degree of the New Generator: n(n-1)/2
content: vandermondePoly_isHomogeneous shows Δ is homogeneous of degree ∑_i |Ioi i|: it is a product of degree-one factors X j - X i (IsHomogeneous.prod, with each factor homogeneous of degree 1 by isHomogeneous_X.sub). vandermondePoly_degree_eq collapses the index sum to closed form: ∑_{i:Fin n} |Ioi i| = ∑_{i:Fin n} (n-1-i) = ∑_{i<n} i = n(n-1)/2 (Fin.card_Ioi, then a Gauss-sum reflection Finset.sum_range_reflect + Finset.sum_range_id). This is C(n,2), the number of pairs i < j — vastly larger than β(Sₙ) = n, exhibiting how sharply the optimal degree jumps from a group to its index-two subgroup.
